correctness.rationale: Exact integer A^7 and A^14 verified. Over F2 the seven nonzero states and seven nonzero first-coordinate rows form single A-orbits; [v,Bv,Cv] is invertible for every nonzero v by its checked base determinant and commutation. The resulting unique r yields step-1 increment 2 (mod4) and 2^j-step increment 2^(j+1) (mod2^(j+2)), j>=1. Induction on binary index digits proves a full even-residue bijection at every 2^k. Scaling handles arbitrary nonzero inputs; zero state is immediate. Standalone verifier replayed all primitive states k<=4, 103 samples k=5 and ten exact lift levels. These finite tests are not substituted for infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Brent implies all primitive vectors have period 7*2^(k-1), covering the originally considered orbit census entirely. The surviving claim instead asserts a congruence-class subsequence is an exact even-residue permutation, including a unique parity-determined progression and zero coverage for scaled initial states. Brent does not assert the needed parity derivatives for the projection; the two separately verified matrices B,C and their mod-two basis give the additional implication. Earlier scalar Perrin valuations and Fibonacci zero-avoidance results do not quantify over these initial states.

value.rationale: The precise natural zero-avoidance question for dyadic Perrin/Padovan recurrences is answered completely, and the proof gives a stronger all-even-residue *permutation*, for every primitive initial triple and every modulus exponent, on an index progression selected by only three parity bits. Uniform output-value coverage is mathematically stronger than a maximum state period and uses separate first-/higher-lift matrices. It contrasts the rich zero-avoidance patterns of second-order Fibonacci modular recurrences and provides a reusable 2-adic value-distribution technique. Scope is only one intrinsic cubic recurrence, no inflated general theorem.
